blocks.text: HTTPX distinguishes connect, read, write and pool timeouts; read and write limits bound waiting for individual chunks rather than a whole request's elapsed duration.

Configure a finite timeout with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=seconds) or a request's timeout= argument; timeout=None disables timeout enforcement. HTTPX raises timeout exceptions such as ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout and PoolTimeout when the corresponding wait exceeds its limit. When the contract requires a total elapsed-time budget across asynchronous work, wrap the operation in async with asyncio.timeout(seconds); its cancellation is converted to TimeoutError outside the context.

edges.label: successive chunks: each wait can fit; total can exceed read limit

blocks.alt_text: Make the shipping lookup's connect, pool, read and write wait boundaries visible alongside a separate total elapsed-time boundary. Show that successive chunks can each arrive within the read limit while total elapsed time exceeds that limit, and distinguish HTTPX timeout exceptions from TimeoutError outside asyncio.timeout.

blocks.text: Configure a finite HTTPX timeout for the shipping lookup. Connect, pool, read, and write have distinct waits; read and write limits apply to individual chunks, not total elapsed time. Timely successive chunks can still extend total duration. For a total budget, use async with asyncio.timeout(seconds) and catch TimeoutError outside the context. Keep that separate from HTTPX timeout exceptions; timeout=None disables enforcement.
